title: SaaS ERP misconceptions: the “on-premises thinking trap”
summary: SaaS ERP deployments often fail when organizations apply on-premises thinking instead of cloud-native practices. The post explains how treating Business Central as a managed service with proper integration patterns, role shifts, and customization discipline delivers value, while recreating on-premises operational models creates unnecessary complexity and cost.
key_points: SaaS misconception: treating cloud ERP as on-premises software deployed elsewhere ignores architectural and operational differences
Upgrade-safe layering in Business Central means extensions survive updates without rework, enabling agility through constraints not limitations
Common deployment errors include centralizing job queue tasks, using polling instead of events, ad-hoc integrations without standards, and test data bloat in production
Best practices: start with accept-as-is default, shift IT roles from infrastructure management to adoption and value, redesign integrations using APIs and events instead of database connections

quotes.text: SaaS is simply on-premises software deployed elsewhere. This fundamentally misses what makes SaaS architecturally and operationally distinct.
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies the core misconception that drives incorrect deployment and operational decisions in SaaS ERP projects

quotes.text: SaaS platforms like Business Central deliver maximum value when treated as continuous, managed services. Applying on-premises rigor creates the worst of both worlds.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the paradox where SaaS pricing with on-premises operations yields poor outcomes and explains why operational model alignment matters
